October 2026 Plan Commission Hearing

NOTE: The October 15th meeting of the Plan Commission hearing will be held at 10:00 AM in City Hall, 121 N. LaSalle St., 11th Floor, Room 1103
Address (Community Area, Ward) Agenda Description Materials (posted by Wednesday, September 30) Draft Presentation (posted by Friday, October 9)

1133 W. Kinzie St.
(Near West Side, 27th Ward)

A proposed Planned Development, submitted by MKR Owner LLC for the property generally located at 1133 W. Kinzie Street. The Applicant requests a rezoning of the subject property from M2-3 to DX-5 to construct a 5-story, 59’-11” residential building with a maximum number of 110 dwelling units, 33 car parking spaces and a maximum FAR of 5.

 PD Application Presentation

3700-3846 N. Seminary Ave.,
1100-1156 W. Grace St., and
3801-3851 N. Racine Ave.
(Lake View, 44th Ward)

A proposed amendment to Institutional Planned Development 108, submitted by Chicago Realty Ventures, LLC, for the property generally located at 3700-3846 N Seminary Avenue, 1100-1156 W Grace Street, and 3801-3851 N Racine Avenue. The applicant proposes amending Planned Development 108 to extend the boundaries of the Planned Development and establish three subareas. The existing surface parking lot in Subarea A is proposed to include up to 800 parking stalls as previously granted via minor change on March 4, 2014. No changes are proposed to Subarea B, which contains an existing public park. Subarea C will include an existing surface parking lot with up to 103 parking spaces. The proposed maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR) of all subareas is 1.2.

 PD Amendment Application Presentation

(7th and 10th Wards)

A resolution seeking the adoption of the South Chicago Land Use Framework plan. This planning effort led by DPD establishes a framework for future land use recommendations in the South Chicago community area in the 7th and 10th wards. It evaluated land use, zoning, community priorities, and redevelopment opportunities in South Chicago, informed by a public engagement process and review of community-led planning initiatives. The recommendations of the land use framework will serve as a planning tool to support strengthening residential areas, foster thriving commercial corridors, and open spaces, and achieve other local priorities
